comparable_contexts.definition:
Comparable contexts: explicit-intent cases where F0 ranks a grade-0 Crime/Thriller title A above the

comparable_contexts.aggregation_note: Mean of per-prediction S(m) across comparable cases; bootstrap resamples MEMBERS (n_boot=2000). This aggregation is our extension, not part of CATGX.

limitations: CATGX-adapted: exact enumeration (no ANN sampling), g(r) by replay, title-activity bins; see ledger.

outputs.units: score = pairwise log-odds; components additive; beh_logit = raw backbone logit

limitations: Component values are fitted model weights x standardised features, not causal contributions.

evidence: Behaviour is the largest component of the A-B margin in this case (+0.303).
Two-event history subset [90710, 90708] carries 87% of the behavioural margin; it beats equal-budget recency and random removal.
Removing it does NOT flip the full-ranker order: relevance and popularity still favour A.
Crime->Crime motif attribution is positive across comparable DEV failures (CI excludes 0).
hypotheses: H1 (testable): the behaviour component is not conditioned on how explicit the query is, so crime-heavy history raises intense titles for a light-mystery request.
H2: popularity also favours A; a history change alone may not fix the ordering.
H3: the text encoder (averaged word vectors) cannot represent 'not too intense' (see negation diagnostic).
caveats: One selected illustrative case; aggregate evidence comes from DEV.

narrative.text: F0 ranks A='Along Came a Spider (2001)' at 1 and judged-relevant B='That Darn Cat! (1965)' at 5. Margin components (score units): behaviour +0.303, relevance +0.080, popularity +0.214. Largest: behaviour.

TemGX-adapted explanation (budget 2) selects ['Inception (2010) [Crime/Thriller]', 'Fight Club (1999) [Crime/Thriller]']. Removing them lowers the behavioural margin from 18.17 to 2.37 (87%); equal-budget recency -2.99, random mean +2.56, attention +6.76. Full-ranker margin +0.597 -> +0.333; order flipped: False.
Controlled replay reproduces the change (margin +0.597 -> +0.333); reset max |diff| = 0.0.

Motif M1 (Crime/Thriller -> Crime/Thriller) in this case: S=10.295266658067703. Across 552 comparable DEV failures: mean S=0.248, 95% member-bootstrap CI [0.104, 0.404], S>0 in 37% of cases with the motif.
Chosen change: history_gate - the case's largest margin component is behaviour and the motif pattern recurs. One mechanism changed; F0 weights frozen.
Trained F1 on DEV: params [1.458, -1.307, -0.708], dev loss 0.5337 -> 0.5026; control Fctrl c=0.782.
DEV: F1-F0 NDCG@10 explicit +0.0018 [-0.0004, 0.004], broad +0.0873 [0.0757, 0.0996]. Selection is fixed now; FINAL is scored once.

FINAL (held-out templates, test period, showcase excluded): F1-F0 NDCG@10 explicit -0.0068 [-0.0096, -0.0041] (n=624 cases/78 members); broad +0.1208 [+0.1018, +0.1407] (n=308 cases/77 members); low-engagement relevant recall@10 (explicit) -0.0070. Control Fctrl explicit +0.0086 [+0.0066, +0.0108] (n=624 cases/78 members), broad -0.0085 [-0.0123, -0.0050] (n=308 cases/77 members).
Primary case under F1: A rank 1, B rank 5 (F0: 1, 5).

Tradeoff, not a win: the gate improves BROAD queries (F0 under-uses history there) but REGRESSES the targeted explicit-intent slice. Do not ship as is. H1 is not supported as the main lever for explicit queries. Next experiment: query-conditioned popularity bound (F2) and a negation-aware text encoder (H2/H3) on the same protocol; keep the gate as a broad-query candidate and inspect the explicit regression cases first. Note: the query-independent control down-weighting does better on explicit queries (+0.0086) but costs broad queries.
